h1: Betong Merlin Hotel — a central Betong stay with an indoor pool and mountain-garden views
intro: Betong Merlin Hotel is a 3-star hotel in the heart of Betong, on Chaiya Chawalit Road. What sets it apart from most Betong hotels is its indoor swimming pool, usable in any weather, paired with mountain and garden views around the building. The location is walkable to the world's largest mailbox, the clock tower and the night market in just a few minutes. It is an affordable hotel where many rooms have recently been renovated, though some older rooms remain. From approx. THB 1,000/night, score 7.4 from 161 reviews.

body.html: Betong Merlin Hotel is a roughly 190-room property in central Betong, on Chaiya Chawalit Road, a short distance from the town centre and the main sights. It has been part of Betong for a long time and has renovated its rooms in batches, so you will find both freshly refurbished rooms and older, original ones. Its fair size means it can comfortably host tour groups and families visiting Betong.

The first thing guests mention is the location. From the hotel it is a short walk to the world's largest mailbox, the Betong clock tower, the night market and the morning dim sum spots Betong is famous for. Convenience stores and restaurants surround the property, so food is easy to find. If you come to Betong mainly to explore the town on foot, photograph the street art and try local food, this location feels genuinely handy, with almost no need to call a car.

"We loved that there's an indoor pool — even when it rained, the kids could still swim. In the evening it's just a few minutes' walk to the night market in front of the hotel, and the morning dim sum is right there too."

The indoor swimming pool is what makes Betong Merlin different. Betong gets frequent rain and cool weather, so an indoor pool can be used every day without worrying about the sky, which suits families travelling with children. Around the building you can also see the mountains and greenery, giving that relaxed valley-town feel. Beyond the pool, there is a traditional Thai massage room, a restaurant and a bar within the property.

On the rooms, let's be straight. The recently renovated rooms earn praise for being clean, comfortable to sleep in and looking notably fresher. But some of the not-yet-renovated rooms draw complaints about worn carpets, a musty smell, incomplete bathroom amenities and toilets or taps that don't work perfectly. Soundproofing between rooms is another point some reviews raise, with noise from the next room or the corridor audible at night. The gap between old and new rooms is fairly clear, so noting a request for a renovated room at booking helps a lot.

Service is reasonable for the price point. Many staff are friendly and helpful, though some reviews mention communication and response speed could improve. One thing to know in advance is that parking is limited, so when the hotel is full or there is an event in town, the lot may not be enough and you may need to park outside. Breakfast is served in the hotel restaurant; reviews say it is filling for the price and includes a few local items to try.

In short, Betong Merlin Hotel is not a luxury hotel, but it is an affordable central choice. Its strengths are the walkable location, the all-weather indoor pool and the mountain-garden surroundings. It suits families and groups on a short Betong trip focused on exploring the town. But if you expect every room to be new and service to match a brand-new hotel, compare it alongside other Betong options and note a request for a renovated room first.

A tip from reading the reviews: specifically request a renovated room at booking, as the difference from the older rooms is clear. If you are driving, arriving a little early makes it easier to get a spot in the hotel lot. And over long weekends and festivals, Thai travellers flock to Betong and the hotel fills quickly, so book ahead and choose a free-cancellation option if your plans aren't fixed yet.

Its strengths are the all-weather indoor pool, mountain-garden views and easy walking access around Betong. But you have to accept that rooms range from old to new, so room quality isn't consistent.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Betong Merlin Hotel

faq.q: Where is Betong Merlin Hotel and what's within walking distance?
faq.a: It is at 333 Chaiya Chawalit Road in central Betong, Yala Province. A few minutes' walk reaches the world's largest mailbox, the Betong clock tower, the night market, the street art and the Mongkhonrit Tunnel. Convenience stores and restaurants surround the hotel, so you can explore the town on foot without calling a car.

faq.q: How much is Betong Merlin and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around THB 1,000/night for a 30 sq m Standard room. A renovated Superior room is about THB 1,300 and a family room around THB 2,000. Prices vary by season and holidays, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does it have a swimming pool, and what kind?
faq.a: Yes, it has an indoor swimming pool, which is a highlight here. Betong rains often and the weather is cool, so the indoor pool can be used in any weather, ideal for families with children. The building is also surrounded by mountains and greenery, giving a valley-town feel.

faq.q: Who is Betong Merlin best for?
faq.a: It suits families, tour groups and travellers exploring Betong on foot who prioritise location and value. It has an indoor pool and free parking. But if you want every room to be new and service to match a brand-new hotel, also compare boutique options in Betong.

Know that rooms range from old to renovated, so quality isn't consistent — requesting a refurbished room at booking is wise. Parking is limited when the hotel is full, so arrive early or ask about backup parking. Over long weekends Thai travellers flock to Betong and the hotel fills quickly, so book ahead.
